item.description: The San Francisco Giants logo is seen on a jersey during the game between the Boston Red Sox and the San Francisco Giants at Fenway Park on Aug. 22, 2026, in Boston. item.title: From DeSoto Speedway to CARS Tour: The Freedom Factory’s Return to Short Track Racing
item.description: Bigley Tune Up Freedom Factory. Photo: Jordan Ashley White A Florida short track that once sat closed is preparing to host one of the country’s most recognizable Late Model racing tours. The Freedom Factory in Bradenton, formerly known as DeSoto Speedway, will host the zMAX CARS Tour’s 2027 season opener on February 6. It marks the series’ first visit to Florida and the latest step in the facility’s return to traditional short-track competition. DeSoto Speedway previously hosted regional and national touring series, including the ASA National Tour and NASCAR Southeast Series. Financial difficulties eventually forced the facility to close in 2018 before automotive YouTuber Cleetus McFarland purchased it in 2020. McFarland initially focused on automotive entertainment, building events around Ford Crown Victorias, burnouts, and other unconventional competitions. But traditional stock car racing has gradually returned, including the Bill Bigley Sr. Memorial 128 and UARA Super Late Model events. The CARS Tour announcement represents another step in that transition. Both the Late Model Stock Car and Pro Late Model divisions will compete on the three-eighths-mile asphalt oval, with Dale Earnhardt Jr., Kevin Harvick, and McFarland among the drivers expected to participate. The event also takes the CARS Tour farther south than ever before, expanding its reach beyond its traditional southeastern racing markets. At a time when other short tracks are struggling with operating costs and uncertain futures, the Freedom Factory offers an example of how a historic facility can find new uses while bringing competitive racing back to its original surface. The CARS Tour season opener is scheduled for February 6, 2027, with coverage on FloRacing.

item.title: Alabama cuts ties with defensive back after latest arrest
item.description: Dec 4, 2015; Atlanta, GA, USA; The Alabama Crimson Tide logo on the playing field at the Georgia Dome in preparation for the SEC Championship Saturday. Mandatory Credit: John David Mercer-USA TODAY Sports The Alabama Crimson Tide faces new controversy as a player has been charged with allegedly harassing a police officer online. As the Tide prepared for their matchup against the Texas A&M Aggies, defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. watched from home after being suspended. However, on Monday, head coach Kalen DeBoer told reporters that Kirkpatrick Jr. was “not with us,” and the program has since cut ties with him amid his pending criminal charges. Kirkpatrick Jr. was charged with harassing communications and doxing, both misdemeanors. DeBoer released a statement on Tuesday announcing the split. “After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program,” DeBoer said in a statement, via ESPN . “He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players.” Kirkpatrick Jr. allegedly sent the officer a profane message that included, “text me back don’t be no b—-!” according to documents obtained by WBRC and The Tuscaloosa Thread. Kirkpatrick allegedly posted a photo of the officer and his family to his Facebook page with the caption, “Dis him?” which caused “severe concern for the overall safety and well-being of himself and his family,” given Kirkpatrick’s “substantial audience and public following” as an Alabama football player, the officer claimed in a criminal complaint, according to TMZ . Kirkpatrick Jr. was arrested last year on three counts of reckless endangerment and one count of attempting to elude and speeding, and he was suspended for the remainder of the 2025 season. The officer he allegedly targeted was involved in that arrest. Kirkpatrick appeared in Alabama’s first seven games of the 2026 season, recording four tackles before his departure. The Kirkpatrick name has rung bells around campus before, as his father, Dre Kirkpatrick, played for the Crimson Tide from 2009 to 2011 and won two national titles. item.title: Brewers' Cooper Pratt Sets Rookie Record In Game 5 Of World Series
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt In Game 4 of the World Series, Cooper Pratt hit a 12th-inning home run that looked like it would get him a mural in Milwaukee, but the Tampa Bay Rays rallied to win the game. However, the home run was simply a part of Pratt's historic hot streak at the plate. In Game 5, he recorded hits in his first two at-bats, setting the record for consecutive at-bats with a hit in a World Series by a rookie, per MLB Network's Sarah Langs . His third time at the plate ended in a sacrifice fly, marking the first time in his last six trips to the plate that he did not get a hit. In Game 4, Pratt lined out in his first plate appearance, but then started his record-setting streak. After that, he went double, single, single and home run in Game 4. He started Game 5 with an RBI single and got a single with one out in the fifth inning. The MLB record for consecutive at-bats with a hit in the World Series belongs to Billy Hatcher, who did it in 1990. David Ortiz, Thurman Munson, Norm Cash and Goose Goslin all reached six like Pratt. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Technically, Pratt's sacrifice fly in his third at-bat of Game 5 did not end his streak since it was not an official at-bat. Pratt's hot streak has come out of nowhere and at the right time. The rookie slashed .281/.350/.368 with three home runs in the regular season. He was seen as a glove-first shortstop, with potential to develop into a plus hitter. That potential is why the Brewers signed him to an eight-year, $50 million deal before he made his debut. He has found success by not trying to do much. He has not hit for many extra bases, but he has used the opposite field well, and finds a way to make an impact on the bases with his speed. This postseason, he has a .869 OPS and could win World Series MVP. He has eight hits, five runs, 13 total bases and seven RBIs in the Fall Classic. item.title: Timberwolves announce disappointing Anthony Edwards injury news
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images Only a week into the 2026-2027 NBA season, Minnesota Timberwolves star guard Anthony Edwards will miss time due to injury. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania , Edwards will miss “up to two months” as he will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee. The seventh-year guard, whom the Timberwolves drafted first overall in 2020, dealt with injuries to both knees last season. He received an MRI on his right knee in March that revealed inflammation, and he also suffered a left knee hyperextension and bone bruise during the Wolves’ first-round playoff series against the Denver Nuggets in April. Edwards averaged 33 points through the first four games of Minnesota’s season as the Wolves sit at 3-1. The pairing of former Charlotte Hornets guard LaMelo Ball and Edwards proved an early success, as the team seemed to mesh well, losing only to the Cleveland Cavaliers in an overtime game on Monday. Edwards was seen grabbing his right knee in Sunday’s win over Toronto and was listed on the injury report Monday. The Timberwolves weren’t too concerned about the injury given the long season, per head coach Chris Finch. “It’s a daily situation,” Finch said, via The Athletic . “I don’t think there’s any long-term concern.” Despite the early setback, Edwards’ business team remains optimistic and confirmed his focus. “Like we’ve talked about before, there’s only one thing that matters to Ant. It’s not about individual accolades, All-NBAs, or anything like that. It’s a single focus — winning a championship,” Justin Holland, Edwards’ business manager, said, via The Athletic . “We’ve seen in a short time what the team is capable of, and know big things are ahead when all are 100 percent.” The Wolves won’t be left in bad hands, as they have several skilled guards who can step up. Ball will take more shots without Edwards and may also get a better feel for the team, as the reins could be in his hands until late December. item.title: Miami stumble to draw against Cincinnati despite Suarez strike
item.description: Luis Suarez scored his team's first goal during the MLS match between Inter Miami CF and FC Cincinnati (Megan Briggs) Lionel Messi's Inter Miami stumbled to a 2-2 draw with Cincinnati on Wednesday in an MLS game that sprang to life after half-time with four superb goals. Miami took the lead with a Luis Suarez strike on the hour mark, but conceded two in quick succession before grabbing back a late equalizer from substitute Riquelme Fillipi to ensure the spoils were shared. The draw was a setback in Miami's pursuit of the Eastern Conference's second seed, as the star-studded side lost ground on the New England Revolution, who beat the New York Red Bulls 3-2. Despite the heartbreak of Fillipi's late strike, the point could prove valuable for Cincinnati, who sit on the cusp of the automatic playoff places, but are currently headed for the wild card round and could yet miss out entirely with two games remaining. In a low-key first half, Miami controlled possession and comprehensively out-passed Cincinnati, but were unable to pierce through. That changed in the 61st minute, as Rodrigo De Paul picked up the ball in the middle of the park, in acres of space, and played it wide to Casemiro. The Brazilian played it first time with the outside of his boot to Suarez, lurking just inside the box. The Uruguayan veteran took one touch, swiveled and perfectly curled the ball into the far top corner, where it crashed down and in off the crossbar. But Cincinnati rallied, and in the 80th minute Frenchman Kenji Mboma Dem scored with another beautiful curling effort to the far post. He picked up the ball wide right, ran at multiple defenders with a flurry of stepovers, then cut inside to score. Just six minutes later, Cincinnati silenced Miami's Nu Stadium by taking the lead. Defender Samuel Gidi received a pass on the edge of the box and wrapped his left foot around the ball, sending it past Dayne St. Clair. With Messi heavily man-marked and unable to get a shot away, De Paul sprayed a wide pass to young Brazilian attacker Fillipi, who cut back to the corner of the box and bent it through two defenders and into the far side of the goal. Both sides had even later chances to win the game, with Suarez blasting his at the goalkeeper before Evander's shot was blocked by a defender at close range as the referee waved away handball appeals. Inter Miami play New England on Sunday, sitting two points back and needing either a win or a draw to keep their hopes of second place alive. Nashville SC are top, and clinched the Supporters' Shield last weekend for the first time in the club's history. amz/bb

item.title: Jesse Love and Justin Allgaier Separated by Just 19 Points Heading Into Martinsville
item.description: Nov 1, 2025; Avondale, Arizona, USA; NASCAR Xfinity Series driver Justin Allgaier (7) leads driver Jesse Love (2) during the Xfinity Series Championship race at Phoenix Raceway. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Only 19 points separate Jesse Love and Justin Allgaier heading into Saturday’s NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series race at Martinsville Speedway, with two races remaining in the 2026 championship battle. Love enters the National Debt Relief 250 leading the standings with 2,401 points, while Allgaier sits second with 2,382. The gap narrowed from 36 points following Talladega, where Love finished third and Allgaier finished fourth after winning Stage 2. Martinsville could provide Allgaier with another opportunity to close the deficit. The JR Motorsports driver won at the half-mile track in March, leading 114 of 250 laps to secure his second career Martinsville victory. Love, meanwhile, has maintained the championship lead despite pressure from the competition. His No. 2 Richard Childress Racing team will also lose pit selection at Martinsville following multiple pre-race inspection failures at Talladega, potentially adding another challenge at a track where pit-road position matters. The championship battle extends beyond the top two drivers. Corey Day trails Love by 29 points, while Sheldon Creed sits 50 points behind and Carson Kvapil is 59 points back. Allgaier has already demonstrated his ability to win at Martinsville this season, but Love remains in control of the standings. Saturday’s race will determine how close the championship fight is when the series heads to Homestead-Miami Speedway. The National Debt Relief 250 begins October 31 at 4 p.m. Eastern on The CW.

item.title: Valtteri Bottas Responds to Cadillac Future Rumors
item.description: Valtteri Bottas has responded to rumors about his future at Cadillac. The Finnish driver, whose performance has been below expectations in recent races, said his 2027 contract is in order and that the team is satisfied with his work. This follows a statement from Marcin Budkowski, director of the American team, who avoided confirming whether his drivers will continue and admitted he had been contacted by several drivers interested in the seat. "Yes, I mean, last year when I signed, I knew the terms, so all that is fine," Bottas declared when asked about the guarantees the team had given him for 2027. The Finn, who has accumulated 264 Formula 1 races, downplayed Budkowski's statements and assured that they don't worry him: "I wasn't aware of those statements and they don't worry me," he added. Bottas's lack of pace, in both qualifying and the race, has fueled speculation about a possible departure from Cadillac. Names like Esteban Ocon, who lost his seat at Haas to Rafael Câmara, test driver Colton Herta, and Red Bull reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda have been mentioned as possible replacements; however, Bottas has remained calm and confident about his future. "I mean, this is Formula 1; if cows flew, you know... anything can happen in this sport, but for now they seem happy with what they are getting from me. I think that is all that matters," the Finn reflected, a response that reflects his experience and his ability to manage pressure in an environment as competitive as Formula 1. Marcin Budkowski, for his part, was evasive when asked about the possibility of Ocon joining the team: "Well, look, as team director, and I am sure it is the same with my colleagues, you receive calls and contacts from every driver or driver manager who is on the market, so there are several drivers and managers who have contacted me. Yankees fans are livid, and they’ve recognized that things are the same; the success line is fading. Baseball analysts have been pinpointing the fact that the Yankees environment has been very relaxed, and not what it used to be. In this case, the main men are Yankees manager Aaron Boone and Yankees general manager Brian Cashman. Fans wanted to see Boone out the door after they were eliminated in the ALDS. Shortly after this, it was announced that Cashman was extended on his contract. Cashman was another figure who Yankees fans were fed up with. Now that all of these deals are established, moving forward is the way to go. Boone and Cashman need to step up to restructure a winning environment, from the front office to the field. This means talent acquisition, lineup configurations, and roster construction. These two leaders need to work together to build a winning environment, as in previous years. Boone played for the Yankees when the team was constructed distinctively.

item.title: Howe, Nagelsmann, Pochettino: can anyone end Manchester United’s doom loop?
item.description: Even an elite coach would surely struggle at Old Trafford amid the executive chaos and with an unfit, uneven squad In January 2014 the 13th series of Celebrity Big Brother aired in the UK, the show so popular that its run time was extended by five days before a public vote anointed Jim Davidson the winner. Then, two years later when Brexit happened, people wondered where their tolerant country had gone, lamenting the ephemeral spirit of London 2012 as though the 2011 riots were some kind of fever dream, not a desperate response to decades of structural and institutional racism exacerbated by the cruelty of unnecessary austerity. The truth is that if security is quickly upended, it was built on quicksand to begin with. Which brings us to Manchester United, easing effortlessly from an uplifting third-place finish to some of the worst football in their history. Continue reading...

As Max Dowman trudged towards the touchline after becoming the youngest player sent off in a League Cup match at 16 years and 300 days, the Arsenal manager could not help himself. Arms folded across his chest like an angry father who has caught his teenage son sneaking in after midnight, Arteta leaned over and aimed a few choice words in Dowman’s direction before the forward headed sheepishly down the tunnel. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
